metadata.title: Remove Global Event Listener Security Vulnerabilities

story.iWant: protection against malicious script injection through event listeners
story.soThat: my data and browsing session remain secure
story.tasks: - [ ] Audit existing global event listeners in video player (AC: 1, 4) - [ ] Scan video player codebase for global event listener usage - [ ] Document all current event listeners and their purposes - [ ] Identify potential security vulnerabilities in current implementation - [ ] Create allowlist of authorized event listeners - [ ] Implement event listener validation middleware (AC: 1, 2) - [ ] Create EventListenerValidator utility class - [ ] Implement allowlist checking for new event listeners - [ ] Add blocking mechanism for unauthorized listeners - [ ] Integrate validation into video player initialization - [ ] Add security event logging and monitoring (AC: 2) - [ ] Implement SecurityEventLogger for suspicious activities - [ ] Create logging integration with WebSocket server - [ ] Add real-time security event monitoring - [ ] Set up alerting for critical security events - [ ] Implement input sanitization for event data (AC: 5) - [ ] Create InputSanitizer utility for event data - [ ] Integrate sanitization into all event handlers - [ ] Add validation for event payload structure - [ ] Test sanitization with various attack vectors - [ ] Update Content Security Policy headers (AC: 3, 6) - [ ] Review current CSP configuration - [ ] Add directives to prevent inline script execution - [ ] Configure CSP for event listener restrictions - [ ] Test CSP effectiveness with security tools - [ ] Security testing and penetration testing (AC: 3, 6) - [ ] Set up OWASP ZAP for automated security scanning - [ ] Perform manual penetration testing on event handling - [ ] Test XSS prevention mechanisms - [ ] Validate CSP header effectiveness - [ ] Document security test results and remediation

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Given video player is initialized, when scripts attempt to add global event listeners, then only authorized listeners are permitted 2. Given suspicious event listeners are detected, when validation runs, then suspicious listeners are blocked and logged 3. Given security testing is performed, when penetration testing is executed, then zero injection vulnerabilities exist in event handling 4. Given video player is running, when event listeners are processed, then all event listeners are properly scoped 5. Given user input is received, when input validation occurs, then input sanitization happens before event processing 6. Given security audit is conducted, when comprehensive testing is performed, then security audit passes penetration testing

constraints.constraint: Security validation must not impact video player performance (<10ms per event)
Must work with existing Video.js event system without breaking functionality
Security utilities should not significantly increase bundle size (<200KB additional)
Security features must work across target browser matrix (Chrome 90+, Safari 14+, Firefox 88+)
Follow existing module patterns in apps/web/src/lib/ for new security utilities
Must integrate with existing WebSocket server for security event logging
